openQuestionResolutions.1-batch-vs-per-page: One convert() call per document, split into per-page strings via textPageSeparator with %page-number%; per-process cache keyed by pdfPath + mtimeMs + size so the frozen per-page surface never spawns a JVM per page. JVM startup measured at ~227 ms; steady-state ~300-670 ms per document.
openQuestionResolutions.2-format: format: 'text' (with keepLineBreaks: true). 'markdown' was rejected for the engine output because ingest already owns table rendering via renderTablesAsMarkdown and text keeps engine output closest to the pdfjs line semantics; 'json' (bounding boxes) deferred as future per-element citation work.
openQuestionResolutions.3-page-counting: pdfjs reuse (cheap, pure JS, no JVM spawn); the opendataloader batch output is validated against the pdfjs count and throws on mismatch (citation provenance depends on it).
openQuestionResolutions.4-distribution: pdfjs kept as the permanent default/fallback engine with zero system dependencies; opendataloader remains strictly opt-in (requires Java 11+). The A/B data supports this (see recommendation).
openQuestionResolutions.5-vendor-benchmarks: Treated as marketing; our corpus is the arbiter. On our corpus opendataloader showed NO content advantage and two table-fidelity regressions.

renderTablesAsMarkdownDecision: OPTION A — the heuristic stays ON for both engines. Evidence (tests/phase-10.test.ts §3.5 test on the tables.pdf corpus fixture): the heuristic only inserts markdown table syntax and never drops or rewrites a word — every whitespace-separated token of both engines' raw output survives rendering; the borderless table is detected under both engines. The opendataloader engine uses format: 'text', so there is no double-processing of engine-emitted markdown tables.

opendataloaderFailures: tables.pdf: drawn grid lines degrade opendataloader's text layer on the bordered table ('West 1430' mangled to 'West 143 0'); only the borderless table detected (3x3) vs. expected 4x3+3x3.
golden-master.pdf: opendataloader inserts a blank line between the table header and data rows, so the heuristic renders the quarter table as 3x3 (Q1 row becomes the header) instead of 4x3.
engineDivergencesRecorded: headers-footers.pdf: opendataloader excludes running headers/footers by default (includeHeaderFooter defaults false); pdfjs includes them. Recorded, not treated as failure.
scanned-page.pdf: BOTH engines extract empty text (OCR gap documented honestly; opendataloader OCR requires the out-of-scope hybrid backend).
abReportHeadline.recommendation: KEEP pdfjs as the default engine. opendataloader passed all expected-string/diacritics/page-alignment checks but failed 2 table-fidelity checks, ran 10.4x slower (4339 ms vs 416 ms total, JVM startup ~227 ms), and adds a hard Java 11+ runtime dependency. Default switch NOT executed — presented to the user for decision (UAT 10.3).
